role_summary: Head of Applied AI for Lattice Inc., a frontier-AI lab building post-training research products. The role partners with the research org on what to ship and owns the engineering side: a small team of senior ICs translating internal model capabilities into customer-facing systems. The hire is the first head-of role for this function — they will define what applied AI means here as much as execute against it.
minimum_bar_description: Ten years of engineering experience with at least four on the application side of frontier ML — fine-tuning, evaluation infrastructure, agent systems, or production RAG. Pure ML-research candidates without applied delivery experience are out of scope; pure ML-platform candidates without product surface area are out of scope.

linkedin.project_name: Head of Applied AI — Lattice Inc.

capability_areas.name: Production agent systems
capability_areas.description: Has shipped LLM-based agentic systems into production, with the operational scar tissue that comes from running them under load. The brief is not looking for prompt-engineers — the hire owns the substrate that makes agents reliable.
builder_signals: Named system in their writing — the agent product, the eval harness, the capability they shipped — described with operational specificity (latency budgets, failure modes, recovery loops).
Trajectory through ML-systems-shaped roles before agents existed; they are not new to production ML, just newly applying it to agents.
Has written publicly about an agent-reliability problem in concrete terms; surfaces in talks, blog posts, or papers.
user_signals: Resume names a popular agent framework as if having used it constitutes ownership.
Heavy on demos and Twitter threads; thin on production deployment evidence.
Career arc that pivoted to agents in the last 12 months from a non-ML domain.

capability_areas.name: Evaluation infrastructure depth
capability_areas.description: Believes evaluation is the hard part. Has built or substantially shaped an evaluation pipeline that the team actually uses to make ship/no-ship calls — not a benchmark for a paper.
builder_signals: Mentions a specific eval system they built and what it changed: a launch they blocked, a regression they caught, a capability they de-risked.
Comfortable with the philosophy fights — distributional vs. behavioral evaluation, pairwise vs. anchor-grounded, synthetic vs. golden — and has a defended position.
Has either authored or substantially shaped an evaluation benchmark that other teams cite.
user_signals: Evaluation is one bullet of many; not load-bearing in their writing.
Talks about "running benchmarks" without distinguishing between a benchmark and a decision-grade eval.
Has only done academic-style evaluation, not production gating.

capability_areas.name: Research-engineering interface fluency
capability_areas.description: The hire sits between research scientists and product engineers. The strongest candidates can read a paper carefully, can ship the implementation, and can argue with the original author about whether the paper applies to the setting they're in.
builder_signals: Co-authored at least one paper at a frontier venue (NeurIPS / ICML / ICLR / ACL); not as the lead author, but as the implementer.
Career history shows tenure on both sides — research-leaning role at one point, product-leaning role at another.
Public artifacts (PRs, posts, talks) that translate research into shipped engineering.
user_signals: Pure research track with no shipping evidence; would be a research scientist hire, not applied AI.
Pure platform track with no research literacy; would be an ML-platform hire, not applied AI.
Heavy reliance on research-author-as-coauthor signal without engineering substance.

depth_distinction.builder_definition: The builder has shipped an applied-AI product whose reliability they personally own. They have a recruiter-readable answer to "which of your products would have been worse without you on it," and the answer cites specific decisions. They read research papers as a working engineer would: which assumption breaks first when this hits production.
depth_distinction.user_definition: The user has consumed applied-AI work without having authored the substrate. They have used internal LLM platforms, fine-tuned models on top of someone else's pipeline, or shipped wrappers around a frontier API. The skills are real but the leverage is at a different layer than this role demands.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: The hardest borderline calls are mid-career engineers with strong systems chops who pivoted to applied AI two years ago and have shipped one substantial product since. If the substrate shows engineering ownership — they wrote the eval harness, they own the agent loop's failure modes — lean save. If they have shipped a wrapper and are growing into the role, lean borderline; the role needs someone who can lead from day one.

non_fit_patterns.label: Pure-research career arc
non_fit_patterns.description: Tenure entirely at research labs with no production-shipping evidence; coauthor list is strong but no products visible.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The role's center of gravity is shipping; a research-only hire would either not get the job done or regret the role within twelve months.

non_fit_patterns.label: Wrapper-only applied AI
non_fit_patterns.description: Applied-AI tenure consists of wrapping a frontier API into a B2B SaaS product without depth on evaluation, fine-tuning, or agent reliability.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The wrapper-shape work is real engineering, but the brief is buying substrate ownership. The candidate would be at the wrong altitude for this team.

non_fit_patterns.label: Manager-only for the past two years
non_fit_patterns.description: Recent role is engineering manager or director without IC contributions; they hired the team that did the work but did not author it.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The role is hands-on for the first eighteen months; a manager-track candidate would slow the team down at exactly the moment it needs to move.

employer_signal_rules.evidence_required: Confirmed tenure on an applied-AI or production-deployment team; pure-research tenure does not count.
Engineering depth visible in scope language; not just product or BD.
ML-platform tenure required; otherwise treat as general-systems prior with applied-AI as a stretch.

minimum_bar: Ten years total engineering experience; four years on applied-AI substrate (evaluation, agents, fine-tuning, or production RAG); demonstrable ownership of a shipped applied-AI product.
